## Scope

This report summarizes **novel (PacBio / `PB*`) isoforms** relative to known transcripts across all configured datasets, then contrasts novelty patterns between the **HT** and **UT** reference transcriptomes.

Novel isoforms are tagged when `oId` starts with the configured prefix (`PB` by default).

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(knitr)
library(dplyr)

# Stay in reports/ so graphic paths ../results/... resolve for pandoc embed-resources.
PROJECT_ROOT <- normalizePath("..", mustWork = TRUE)
tab <- function(...) file.path(PROJECT_ROOT, "results", "tables", ...)
fig <- function(...) file.path("..", "results", "figures", "novel", ...)
```

```{r}
#| label: load-data
need <- c(
  "novel_isoform_dataset_summary.csv",
  "novel_isoform_HT_vs_UT_summary.csv",
  "novel_involved_genes_HT_vs_UT_overlap_summary.csv",
  "novel_involved_genes_shared_HT_UT.csv",
  "top_novel_switching_genes.csv",
  "top_novel_switching_isoforms.csv",
  "novel_isoform_class_code_counts.csv"
)
need_abs <- vapply(need, tab, character(1))
miss <- need_abs[!file.exists(need_abs)]
if (length(miss)) {
  stop(
    "Missing novel analysis outputs. Run: Rscript scripts/03_novel_isoform_analysis.R\n",
    paste(miss, collapse = "\n")
  )
}

ds <- read.csv(need_abs[[1]], stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
ref <- read.csv(need_abs[[2]], stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
ov <- read.csv(need_abs[[3]], stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
shared <- read.csv(need_abs[[4]], stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
top_genes <- read.csv(need_abs[[5]], stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
top_iso <- read.csv(need_abs[[6]], stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
cc <- read.csv(need_abs[[7]], stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
```

## Top novel switching events

### Top novel switching genes (top 15 per dataset)

```{r}
top_g_show <- top_genes |>
  group_by(.data$dataset_label) |>
  slice_head(n = 15) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(
    dataset_label, rank, gene_name, gene_id,
    n_novel_switching_isoforms, max_abs_dif_novel_switching, min_novel_switch_q
  )
knitr::kable(top_g_show, digits = 4, caption = "Top novel-involved switching genes")
```

### Top novel switching isoforms (top 10 per dataset)

```{r}
top_i_show <- top_iso |>
  group_by(.data$dataset_label) |>
  slice_head(n = 10) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(
    dataset_label, gene_name, isoform_id, oId, class_code,
    dIF, abs_dIF, isoform_switch_q
  )
knitr::kable(top_i_show, digits = 4, caption = "Top novel switching isoforms")
```

## HT vs UT contrast panel

This panel aggregates datasets by `reference_transcriptome` (HT vs UT) and compares novelty burden, then asks which **gene symbols** with novel involvement appear in both references.

### Aggregated HT vs UT rates

```{r}
knitr::kable(ref, digits = 2, caption = "HT vs UT novelty summary")
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "HT vs UT percent novel isoforms"
knitr::include_graphics(fig("fig_novel_HT_vs_UT_pct_isoforms.png"))
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "HT vs UT percent novel among switching isoforms"
knitr::include_graphics(fig("fig_novel_HT_vs_UT_pct_among_switching.png"))
```

### Novel-involved gene-symbol overlap

```{r}
knitr::kable(ov, digits = 0, caption = "Overlap of novel-involved gene symbols (HT vs UT)")
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Shared vs reference-specific novel-involved genes"
knitr::include_graphics(fig("fig_novel_HT_vs_UT_gene_overlap.png"))
```

### Shared novel-involved genes (top by HT effect size)

```{r}
shared_show <- shared |>
  arrange(desc(.data$max_abs_dif_novel_switching_HT), desc(.data$max_abs_dif_novel_switching_UT)) |>
  head(40)
knitr::kable(
  shared_show,
  digits = 4,
  caption = "Shared novel-involved gene symbols across HT and UT (first 40)"
)
```

## Notes

- Overlap uses **gene symbols**, because `XLOC_*` / ISA gene IDs are transcriptome-specific.
- “Novel involved” means at least one significant switching isoform is tagged PacBio novel under config q / |dIF| cutoffs.
- Rebuild with:

```bash
Rscript scripts/03_novel_isoform_analysis.R
quarto render reports/novel_isoform_analysis.qmd
```
